source.title: Sleep preferentially consolidates negative aspects of human memory: Well-powered evidence from two large online experiments.
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

confidence_rationale: The strongest source in this pull and the one that most directly evidences a specificity RATIO rising across sleep: negative emotional objects are retained at the expense of their paired neutral backgrounds. Two large samples (250+), explicitly designed as a well-powered replication answering the underpowering criticism levelled at this literature, published in PNAS. Confidence is held at 0.72 rather than higher because the design is an online behavioural sleep-versus-wake delay with no polysomnography -- so it cannot attribute the effect to a sleep PHASE or to any particular operation within one -- and because scene memory is a looser analogue of a residue field than the claim's readouts assume.
failure_signatures: The trade-off is asymmetric: the effect held for negative material but sleep did NOT modulate the corresponding advantage for positive material, so the mechanism is valence-specific rather than a general salience-weighted consolidation -- MECH-018 as written does not predict that asymmetry and does not explain it.

The 'at the expense of' framing means the specificity ratio rises partly because the NEUTRAL term falls, not only because the harm term is held up. A residue field could reproduce this by attenuating everything and attenuating non-harm regions slightly faster, which would pass the specificity-ratio readout while failing the preservation floor -- the two readouts must be scored jointly, not in sequence.

No polysomnography: the paper cannot say the effect belongs to REM, SWS, or to any operation running inside a cycle, so it cannot adjudicate MECH-018's SUBSTRATE question of whether the integration call site is doing the work.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Across two large online experiments (250+ participants), sleep selectively benefited memory for negative emotional objects at the expense of their paired neutral backgrounds, confirming a sleep-specific benefit for negative information; in a second experiment, participants remembered positive objects better than their neutral backgrounds, but sleep did not modulate that effect.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the closest human-behavioural analogue of MECH-018's pre-registered CONTEXT-TYING readout (ii) and its PRESERVATION readout (i) measured jointly. The emotional object is the harm context; the paired neutral background is the equidistant matched non-harm context. The finding is that the ratio between them RISES across sleep and does not rise across an equivalent waking interval -- which is exactly the specificity-ratio gain MECH-018 predicts and exactly what a naive uniform-decay comparator cannot produce.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Object-on-background scene memory is a two-item associative structure; REE's residue is a continuous RBF field whose over-generalisation arises from kernel overlap between neighbouring z_world locations. The paper's 'background' is paired with the object by experimental construction, not by metric proximity in a latent space, so the geometry that makes REE's over-generalisation problem hard is not the geometry being tested. The result also concerns item recognition, not an aversive cost, so 'memory retained' and 'residue preserved' are related but distinct quantities.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adults across a range of ages and backgrounds; online scene-memory task; sleep-versus-wake delay design without polysomnography; two experiments, negative and positive valence respectively.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality is high and deliberately so -- this paper exists to answer the charge that the sleep/emotional-memory literature is underpowered, and it is the replication that charge asked for. Mapping fidelity is the binding constraint.
